intro: most inner voices lean on a few habits. none of them are flaws. each one is trying to help, in its own way.
note: these habits come from "thinking traps" in cognitive behavioral therapy. the voice check is for noticing, not a diagnosis.

habits.name: the rule keeper
says: i should be further along by now.
i should have known better.
i have to get this perfect.
quiz: i should be further along by now.
i should have known better.
habits.job: holds you to a standard, so you keep going.
habits.misses: where the rule came from, and whether it still fits your life.

spot.scene: you finish a long week. you got a lot done. one email is still unanswered.
spot.quote: i should have answered that on tuesday.

answers.line: i'd like to answer it. it's not urgent.
i didn't get to it, and i got a lot of other things done.
hey, you're allowed to be one email behind.

habits.keep: "should" is often a rule someone handed you. you get to check if it's still yours.
habits.try: next time you hear "i should," try swapping it for "i'd like to" and notice what changes.

habits.name: the mind reader
says: they're probably annoyed with me.
they only invited me to be nice.
everyone noticed.
quiz: they're probably annoyed with me.
they only invited me to be nice.
habits.job: tries to stay one step ahead of what people think, so you're never caught off guard.
habits.misses: that you can't actually see inside anyone's head, and neither can it.

spot.scene: a friend replies to your long message with just "ok".

answers.line: the thought says they're done with me. what i actually know is they replied.
i'm noticing the thought that they're done with me.
hey, you don't have to solve this tonight. you could just ask.

habits.keep: a guess about someone else's mind is still a guess. you're allowed to check.
habits.try: catch one mind-read today. ask yourself: what do i actually know?

habits.name: the always-never
says: i always mess things up.
this never works out for me.
nothing ever changes.
quiz: i always mess things up.
nothing ever works out for me.
habits.job: turns one moment into a rule, so you'll see it coming next time.
habits.misses: all the times it went differently.

spot.scene: you burn dinner while texting someone.

answers.line: i burned dinner, and i've made a lot of good dinners.
i'm a little annoyed. it's one dinner.
tonight didn't go how i wanted, for now.

habits.keep: one time is one time. "always" and "never" are rarely the whole story.
habits.try: when you hear "always" or "never" today, try "this time" instead.

habits.name: the forecaster
says: this is going to go terribly.
if i say something, it'll be a disaster.
i'll never be able to handle that.
quiz: this is going to go terribly.
if i say something, it'll be a disaster.
habits.job: prepares you for the worst, just in case.
habits.misses: the other ways it could go, and how often you've coped before.

spot.scene: your manager asks for "a quick chat tomorrow".

answers.line: the thought says i'm getting fired. what i actually know is they want to talk.
what actually happened was a calendar invite. one small next step is asking what it's about.
hey, you've walked into hard conversations before. you can do this one.

habits.keep: a forecast isn't the weather. it's one guess about tomorrow.
habits.try: write down one worry today. look at it again in a week and see how it went.

habits.name: the comparer
says: everyone else has it together.
they're so far ahead of me.
i'm the only one struggling.
quiz: everyone else has it together.
they're so far ahead of me.
habits.job: measures where you stand, so you don't fall behind.
habits.misses: that you're comparing your inside to everyone else's outside.

spot.scene: you scroll past an old classmate's wedding, house, and new job.

answers.line: this is hard. other people feel this too. what i need right now is to put the phone down.
they're doing well, and i'm on my own timeline.
i'm noticing the thought that i'm behind.

habits.keep: you only ever see other people's highlights. you see all of your own footage.
habits.try: notice one comparison today. ask: compared to what, exactly?

habits.name: the labeler
says: i'm such an idiot.
i'm a failure.
i'm too much.
quiz: i'm such an idiot.
i'm too much.
habits.job: sums you up in one word, so things feel simple and clear.
habits.misses: that you're a person who did one thing, not a word.

spot.scene: you forget a coworker's name, right as you introduce them.

answers.line: i'm really embarrassed. that happens to everyone.
if a friend said "i'm such an idiot" about themselves, i'd tell them it was one awkward moment.
hey, you blanked on a name. you're still you.

habits.keep: you did a thing. you're not the thing.
habits.try: when a label shows up, try describing what you did instead of who you are.

habits.name: the discounter
says: that doesn't count, anyone could do it.
they're just being nice.
i got lucky.
quiz: that doesn't count, anyone could have done it.
they're just being nice.
habits.job: keeps you humble, so you keep trying and nobody thinks you're full of yourself.
habits.misses: the good things that are actually true.

spot.scene: your friend says your presentation was really clear.

answers.line: maybe they're being nice, and maybe it was clear.
the thought says they're just being nice. what i actually know is i prepared for it.
hey, you can let that one land.

habits.keep: you're allowed to keep the good stuff too.
habits.try: next time someone compliments you, just say "thank you" and stop there.

habits.name: the it's-on-me
says: it's my fault they're upset.
if i'd done more, this wouldn't have happened.
i ruined the night.
quiz: it's my fault they're upset.
if i'd done more, this wouldn't have happened.
habits.job: looks for what you can control, so you can make things right.
habits.misses: everything else that was going on, that had nothing to do with you.

spot.scene: your partner comes home quiet and goes straight to bed.

answers.line: the thought says i did something. what i actually know is they went to bed early.
what actually happened was they went to bed early. one small next step is asking how they are tomorrow.
this is hard. other people feel this too. what i need right now is to let it rest until morning.

habits.keep: you matter to the people around you. you're not the cause of everything they feel.
habits.try: when you feel responsible for someone's mood, list three other things that could be going on for them.

habits.name: the all-or-nothing
says: if it's not perfect, it's a failure.
i missed one day, so the whole thing is ruined.
either i do it right or not at all.
quiz: if it's not perfect, it's a failure.
i missed one day, so the whole thing is ruined.
habits.job: keeps the bar high, so you aim for your best.
habits.misses: everything in between, which is where most of life happens.

spot.scene: you planned to work out four times this week. you went twice.

answers.line: i'm a little disappointed. twice is more than zero.
i went twice, and i can go again tomorrow.
this week was two, for now.

habits.keep: between all and nothing there's a lot of "some". some counts.
habits.try: pick one thing today and aim for "good enough" on purpose.

habits.name: the feeling-as-fact
says: i feel stupid, so i must be.
it feels like they don't want me there, so they don't.
it feels impossible, so it is.
quiz: i feel stupid, so i must be.
it feels impossible, so it must be.
habits.job: takes your feelings seriously, which matters.
habits.misses: that a feeling tells you how things feel, not always how things are.

spot.scene: you ask a friend for help moving, and feel uneasy about it all day.

answers.line: i'm noticing the feeling that i'm in the way.
i feel like i'm in the way, and they said yes.
if a friend said "i'm just in the way" about themselves, i'd tell them i'm glad they asked.

habits.keep: feelings are real information. they're not always the whole truth.
habits.try: when a big feeling shows up, name it, then ask: what else is true right now?

evidence: well established as a way to describe thinking, from cognitive behavioral therapy
